_doc: The game-feel config for one project: <root>/feel/feel.json (the skill copies this template there on the first run). Every name the harness needs to touch the game is here, so measure.gd never names a project class: it instances the player scene from this path, presses the input actions named here, grants the kit through the autoload named here and calls methods by name. A project that spells things differently edits this file, not the script.

game: the Godot project folder, relative to the root. godot: the binary. player_scene: the player scene the harness instances alone in a greybox fixture; it must stand on the world layer without a room around it.

knobs: the resources the controller reads its numbers from, by group: resource (the .tres, relative to the game folder, the adapter reads it and tune.py --apply writes one line of it) and on_player (the exported property on the player node that holds it, where a `--set` override is applied in memory). A knob name is looked up group by group; the first resource that has the property takes it.

actions: the input actions the harness presses, by role. flags: the autoload and method that grant a kit flag, and `all`: every flag the full kit needs (the harness measures the whole kit; possession is the level-designer's problem).

methods: what the harness calls on the player by role. state_name: the current state's name (for the samples). knockback: the method the hurt pipeline calls with an impulse Vector2 (the knockback probe calls it directly; empty to skip the probe).
bus: the autoload that carries the signals, and hitstop: the signal that requests a freeze in frames (the hitstop probe emits it; empty to skip the probe).

world_layer: the physics layer the fixtures' solids sit on, the one the player collides with. arena: floor_y is the floor's top face in world px; settle_frames is how long the player is left alone between trials so every timer runs out (longer than the longest cooldown).

reach: the level-designer's reach.json, relative to the root, to judge the measured reach against the model. district: its district.json, for the tile size. scale: the bible's scale.json (grid_unit_art_px x world_px_per_art_px) when there is no district. tile_px: the tile size outright, when neither file has it.

probes: per-probe numbers. drop_height: the fall the buffer and landing probes drop from. fall_height: the drop that reaches terminal velocity. shaft_widths: the shaft widths the climb is tried in (inner faces, px). knockback_impulse: the impulse the knockback probe calls with (its sign is the direction; the magnitude is the player's own). hitstop_frames: the light and heavy holds requested, when controller.json does not carry them.
